title: Potato, baked, peel not eaten, with meat

content.title: About
content.content: Baked potato without the edible peel, served with meat, is a popular dish in Russian cuisine. The potato is boiled until tender, then baked to a golden crust, and the peel is removed to obtain a soft, fluffy interior. Meat such as beef, pork, or chicken, seasoned with spices, is added on top.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Baking enhances the natural sweetness of potatoes through caramelization of sugars.
Potato skin contains more fiber and vitamins, but this dish intentionally discards it.
Traditionally served in colder months as a hearty lunch or dinner.
The combination of potato and meat provides a complete set of carbs and proteins.
In Russia, baked potatoes are often accompanied by sour cream and fresh herbs.

items.title: Source of complex carbohydrates
items.content: Potatoes provide slow‑releasing energy, helping to maintain stable blood sugar levels.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C supports immune function and improves iron absorption from the meat.

items.title: Contains potassium
items.content: Potassium aids in blood pressure regulation and muscle function.

items.title: Protein from meat
items.content: Meat adds complete protein necessary for tissue repair and growth.

items.title: Low in fat when prepared correctly
items.content: Baking without excessive oil keeps saturated fat content low.

items.title: Meat allergy
items.content: Some individuals may be allergic to certain types of meat and should exercise caution.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Over‑salting during baking can increase the risk of hypertension.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: Potatoes have a high glycemic index; people with diabetes should monitor portion size.

items.title: Potential pathogens
items.content: Undercooked meat can harbor bacteria, so ensure it is cooked to a safe internal temperature.

items.title: Loss of nutrients in the peel
items.content: Removing the skin reduces fiber and some vitamins, so compensate with other nutrient‑rich foods.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the baked potato split open, topped with sautéed meat pieces, sprinkled with herbs and seasoned with spices. Add sour cream, grated cheese, or tomato sauce to taste.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the prepared dish in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2‑3 days. Reheat in the oven or microwave to an internal temperature above 75 °C before serving.
